findings.title: Dynamic import of user-reachable arch.ts executes arbitrary code in daemon process
findings.detail: InvariantRunner.runArch() calls import(pathToFileURL(targetPath).href) on worker-writable .ifleet/invariants/<repoSlug>/arch.ts. A jailbroken worker can write a malicious arch.ts that gets dynamically imported by the daemon process under full process credentials. The path-traversal check blocks .. and absolute paths but not file-content attacks.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace dynamic import with a sandboxed worker_threads runner or vm.runInContext with a restricted module loader. Allowlist which repos can declare arch.ts in config and validate file content before importing.

findings.title: TLS verification disabled for Supabase/PostgreSQL when CA cert path is not set
findings.detail: When SUPABASE_CA_CERT_PATH is unset and the URL contains 'supabase.co', the pool is created with ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false }, disabling certificate validation on connections carrying knowledge-graph embeddings and audit findings. Trivially vulnerable to MITM interception.
findings.fix_sketch: Require SUPABASE_CA_CERT_PATH in production or use ssl: true (system CA bundle) instead of disabling verification. Throw or warn loudly and refuse pool creation when NODE_ENV=production and cert is absent.

findings.title: Public control plane cancel only marks store state; running pipeline worker is NOT killed
findings.detail: The onCancel handler on port 3001 writes blocked+cancelled to TaskStore but does NOT abort the in-flight pipeline worker (AbortController lives only in the daemon on port 3002). Operators receive HTTP 202 OK believing the task is cancelled while Claude continues consuming API quota and making commits. No timeout or watcher eventually kills the orphaned worker.
findings.fix_sketch: Route cancel commands exclusively to port 3002, or add a daemon watcher that notices blocked+cancelled in the store and triggers AbortController.abort() for the pipeline.

findings.title: Docker sandbox runs as --user root inside every container
findings.detail: buildDockerArgs() hard-codes --user root for all verification phases. A container-escape vulnerability gives an attacker root credentials on the host. The worktree is mounted at /work so file exfiltration is already possible post-escape.
findings.fix_sketch: Create a dedicated non-root user in the ifleet-verifier:base Docker image and use --user ifleet (UID 1000). Change /root/.pnpm-store to /home/ifleet/.pnpm-store in the image accordingly.

findings.title: Editor reviewer and doctor roles receive architect output as direct Claude instructions with no injection filter
findings.detail: In buildWorkerPool.spawn(), trustedBrief=true for all non-architect roles skips wrapBriefAsData(). If the architect is jailbroken or returns malicious output, that content becomes direct instructions for editor/reviewer/doctor with no sandboxing.
findings.fix_sketch: Apply a lightweight quoteAsUserData() wrapper to architect output before forwarding to editor/reviewer/doctor, or validate architect output conforms to expected JSON plan schema before passing it downstream.

findings.title: GitHub token exposed via git -c argument visible in proc cmdline and ps output
findings.detail: authPrefix() injects the GitHub token as -c http.https://github.com/.extraheader=AUTHORIZATION: bearer <TOKEN>. This argument is visible in /proc/<pid>/cmdline and to logging tools that capture command lines.
findings.fix_sketch: Use GIT_ASKPASS or a credential helper script that reads the token from a file. This keeps the token out of argv.

findings.title: Bash cat glob in worker allow list can exfiltrate arbitrary host files
findings.detail: The WORKER_CLAUDE_PERMISSIONS allow list includes Bash(cat *) with no path restriction. A worker can cat /etc/passwd, cat ~/.claude/credentials.json, or traverse to parent directories to read host-level secrets.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace Bash(cat *) with Bash(cat ./*) or restrict to the worktree path. Better yet remove cat from the allow list and rely on the Read tool (already allowed) for file reading.

findings.title: markCancelled in UnifiedQueueAdapter missing conditional fromState guard
findings.detail: markCompleted and markFailed pass fromState='in_flight' to store.updateState() so concurrent state changes are detected. markCancelled calls store.updateState without a fromState guard, meaning a completed or failed task can be overwritten with blocked+cancelled, corrupting the audit trail.
findings.fix_sketch: Add fromState='in_flight' as the fourth argument to store.updateState() in markCancelled, and check the returned boolean to skip sourceFor(task).markFailed() when the state was not updated.

findings.title: markFindingClosed writes index.json and closed.json non-atomically
findings.detail: markFindingClosed() calls writeAuditIndex first then appendToClosedJson separately without holding the index.json lock across both operations. A process crash between writes leaves index.json showing the finding as closed but closed.json missing the record.
findings.fix_sketch: Combine the index.json write and the closed.json append inside a single withClosedJsonLock critical section.

findings.title: GitHub drain loop has premature break on duplicate ID before exclusion set insertion
findings.detail: In GitHubIssuesSource.drain(), after pickNext the code checks if (exclude.has(next.id)) break before adding the ID to the exclude set. This causes the drain loop to terminate instead of continuing when pickNext returns a previously-seen ID.
findings.fix_sketch: Move exclude.add(next.id) to before the if (exclude.has(next.id)) break check, or remove the redundant guard since excludeIds handles dedup at the source.

findings.title: getAllPrDecisions defaults to 50000 rows with no streaming
findings.detail: TaskStore.getAllPrDecisions() defaults to limit=50000 rows fetched synchronously via better-sqlite3 all(). Loads all rows into a single JS array before returning, potentially consuming hundreds of MB of heap.
findings.fix_sketch: Add pagination with a before cursor on created_at or use iterate() to stream rows. Cap default at 1000.

findings.title: MemoryNonceLedger setInterval timer not unref-ed causing Node.js process hang in tests
findings.detail: MemoryNonceLedger starts a setInterval in its constructor. Tests that create a control plane but fail to call stop() leak the interval timer, preventing Node.js from exiting after the test suite completes.
findings.fix_sketch: Add .unref() on the interval timer so it does not prevent Node.js from exiting when no other work is pending.

findings.title: Discord broadcast messages silently dropped with no dead-letter log when outbox not configured
findings.detail: In broadcastIFleet(), when pendingCount >= MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH and _outbox is null, the message is dropped with only a console.warn. The outbox is not wired on the public control-plane process. Burst events during bot restart or Discord downtime are silently lost.
findings.fix_sketch: Record dropped messages to a persistent dead-letter log. Alternatively wire the outbox to the public server as well as the daemon.

findings.title: repoSlug hardcoded to IFleet in VerifierController preventing multi-repo invariant checking
findings.detail: In daemon.ts the VerifierController is constructed with repoSlug: 'IFleet' hardcoded. Invariants for any other managed repo are never run regardless of which repo the task targets.
findings.fix_sketch: Thread the task's repo field through VerifierController so repoSlug is derived from the task being verified rather than fixed at boot.

findings.title: Package imports cross package boundary via deep relative path traversals
findings.detail: interaction-create.ts imports ../../../../../src/audit/audit-store.js and ../../../../../src/orchestrator/approval-gate.js, escaping packages/orchestrator-core/ into main src/. Breaks monorepo isolation and creates fragile path resolution.
findings.fix_sketch: Expose required functions as a proper package dependency replacing relative path escapes with package imports.

findings.title: node_modules symlink in worktree allows workers to install packages affecting all concurrent tasks
findings.detail: setupWorktree() creates a symlink from worktree/node_modules to repoRoot/node_modules. Workers with Bash(pnpm *) can run pnpm install which resolves through the symlink to shared host node_modules, affecting all concurrent tasks in other worktrees.
findings.fix_sketch: Deny Bash(pnpm install *) specifically in the worker deny list, or use a per-worktree copy of node_modules rather than a symlink.

findings.title: wrapBriefAsData does not scrub BRIEF_DATA_MARKER_OPEN from user input enabling nested block injection
findings.detail: wrapBriefAsData() scrubs BRIEF_DATA_MARKER_CLOSE from user-supplied content but not BRIEF_DATA_MARKER_OPEN. An adversarial user can include the open marker to create confusing nested block structure, potentially causing the model to treat instruction-layer text as data.
findings.fix_sketch: Also scrub BRIEF_DATA_MARKER_OPEN from user input alongside the existing BRIEF_DATA_MARKER_CLOSE scrub.

findings.title: spawnCapture passes full process.env minus GIT_ vars exposing secrets to git subprocess hooks
findings.detail: spawnCapture() in repos/manager.ts passes most of process.env (including GITHUB_TOKEN, DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN, IFLEET_HMAC_SECRET) to the git subprocess, visible to any pre/post-commit hooks or credential helpers git invokes.
findings.fix_sketch: Apply the same minimal env allowlist used in claudeChildEnv() and verifyChildEnv(): pass only HOME, PATH, USER, LOGNAME, LANG, and required GIT_ auth vars.

findings.title: getKgPool caches pool module-level with no connection error handler
findings.detail: There is no pool.on('error', ...) handler on the cached pg Pool. Idle client errors cause unhandled promise rejections that can crash the daemon process.
findings.fix_sketch: Add cachedPool.on('error', (err) => console.error('[kg-pool] idle client error:', err)) after creating the pool.

findings.title: DiscordOutbox table DDL duplicated between discord-outbox.ts and store.ts SCHEMA risking silent drift
findings.detail: The discord_outbox table DDL appears in both packages/orchestrator-core/src/observability/discord-outbox.ts and packages/orchestrator-core/src/queue/store.ts SCHEMA. Schema drift between the two DDL strings would silently fail to apply the newer definition to existing databases.
findings.fix_sketch: Remove the discord_outbox DDL from TaskStore SCHEMA and let DiscordOutbox own it entirely.

findings.title: verify and force_pr commands silently no-op on public control plane returning false 202 success
findings.detail: The onVerify and onForcePr handlers on the public server log to stderr but return undefined, while the HTTP layer still responds HTTP 202. The Discord bot tells the operator the command was accepted when it had no effect.
findings.fix_sketch: Return HTTP 503 with a descriptive body from these handlers on the public server, or remove them from the public server entirely.

findings.title: Verifier docker image ifleet-verifier:base assumed to exist with no build or pull probe at startup
findings.detail: DockerSandboxRunner defaults to image: 'ifleet-verifier:base' and never validates the image exists before running verification phases. If the image is missing, every phase fails with a cryptic Docker error.
findings.fix_sketch: Add an imageExists probe in probeDocker() and surface a clear error when the image is absent. Add a build/pull step to the VPS deployment script.

findings.title: ControlPlane HTTP server destroys nonce store before draining in-flight connections
findings.detail: In createControlPlane(), stop() calls nonceStore.destroy() synchronously before server.close(). In-flight requests at shutdown may call nonceStore.registerOrReject() after the ledger is torn down: for MemoryNonceLedger nonce dedup is silently disabled; for SqliteNonceLedger calls to a closed DB throw.
findings.fix_sketch: Call nonceStore.destroy() only after server.close() resolves (inside the close callback), ensuring all in-flight requests complete before the nonce store is torn down.

findings.title: pendingCount derived from stale in-memory snapshot can trigger spurious rate-pause
findings.detail: Line 356 of sprint.ts used tasks (the pre-dispatch snapshot) instead of freshTasks (loaded after dispatch loop) to count pending tasks. After dispatch transitions tasks to assigned, the stale snapshot still shows them as pending, triggering checkRateLimit unnecessarily.
findings.fix_sketch: Use freshTasks.filter() instead of tasks.filter() on line 356. Fixed in this audit run.

findings.title: durationMs inflated by pause time when sprint is paused and resumed before completing
findings.detail: sprint.completed payload computed durationMs as now - running.startedAt. Since startedAt is the original start time (preserved through pause/resume cycles), the metric includes all pause time. Added elapsedMs tracking to accumulate only active time.
findings.fix_sketch: Track elapsedMs in running/paused states; compute durationMs as (elapsedMs ?? 0) + (now - startedAt) where startedAt resets to now() on each resume. Fixed in this audit run.

findings.title: console.warn used for routine informational log messages throughout server.ts and daemon.ts
findings.detail: Both src/server.ts and src/orchestrator/daemon.ts use console.warn for normal startup messages. PM2 routes stderr separately from stdout, so these appear as warnings in PM2 logs causing noise and masking real warnings.
findings.fix_sketch: Use console.log for informational messages and reserve console.warn for genuinely unexpected but non-fatal conditions.

findings.title: TaskSource interface has no markCancelled causing cancelled tasks to appear as failed in GitHub and Discord
findings.detail: UnifiedQueueAdapter.markCancelled() calls sourceFor(task).markFailed() because TaskSource has no markCancelled method. GitHub issues and Discord threads receive a failed label even when the task was deliberately cancelled.
findings.fix_sketch: Add markCancelled(task: QueuedTask, reason: string): Promise<void> to the TaskSource interface and implement it in both GitHubIssuesSource and DiscordSource.

findings.title: Silently swallowed errors in void fire-and-forget chains in repos/manager.ts
findings.detail: packages/orchestrator-core/src/repos/manager.ts uses void settled.then(...) with no .catch() on some call sites, silently swallowing errors from lock cleanup logic.
findings.fix_sketch: Add explicit .catch((err) => console.error('[repo-manager] lock cleanup error:', err)) after settled.then() call sites.

findings.title: apps/wahq-bot/src/index.ts is an empty stub with only an export statement
findings.detail: The file contains only export {} with no implementation or roadmap reference, creating an empty package entrypoint that could confuse future contributors.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a comment explaining this is a stub pending the Agent SDK migration (referencing AGENTS.md).

findings.title: onApprove handler returns void — misrouted approvals silently succeed
findings.detail: In src/server.ts, onApprove logged an error but returned void. The control plane saw a resolved handler and returned HTTP 202 Accepted. Operators routing /approve to port 3001 got a success response while the task remained blocked in architect wait state.
findings.fix_sketch: Mirror onCancel: throw new Error('approve is daemon-only; route to CONTROL_PLANE_PORT 3002'). FIXED.

findings.title: git commit failure swallowed in editor — caller sees misleading no-diff error
findings.detail: In src/pipeline/editor.ts, failed git commit only emitted console.warn and returned normally. The caller computed no committed diff and logged a misleading 'editor produced no diff — possible silent tool-use failure'. The actual commit error was hidden.
findings.fix_sketch: Re-throw on commit failure: same pattern as AUDIT-IFleet-e5f6a7b8 for git add. FIXED.

findings.title: runTickLoop fire-and-forget void — unhandled rejection silently terminates daemon
findings.detail: In src/orchestrator/daemon.ts, void runTickLoop(...) had no .catch() handler. In Node.js 15+, an unhandled promise rejection from the tick loop causes a fatal process crash with no logged context.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace void with .catch((err) => { console.error(...); process.exit(1); }). FIXED.

findings.title: DockerSandboxRunner runCommand inherits full process.env including all secrets
findings.detail: In src/agents/verifier/sandbox.ts, runCommand() created SpawnOptions without setting env, so git clone/checkout and docker subprocesses inherited the full daemon process.env including ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, IFLEET_HMAC_SECRET, and GITHUB_TOKEN.
findings.fix_sketch: Apply env: verifyChildEnv() to SpawnOptions in DockerSandboxRunner.runCommand. FIXED.

findings.title: discardRawLog exported but never called — verifier temp dirs accumulate indefinitely
findings.detail: In src/agents/verifier/sandbox.ts, uploadLog() creates a mkdtemp directory per verifier run. discardRawLog() was exported as the cleanup function but had no call sites. On long-running daemons, /tmp filled with ifleet-verifier-* directories.
findings.fix_sketch: Import discardRawLog in controller.ts and call it after bridge.completeRun(merged). FIXED.

findings.title: handleAuditFix catch block swallows dispatch error — failure reason invisible
findings.detail: In packages/orchestrator-core/src/discord/handlers/interaction-create.ts, the catch block on controlPlane.postCommand discarded the error entirely. Discord reported a count of failed findings but no reason.
findings.fix_sketch: Log the caught error before pushing to failed array. FIXED.

findings.title: MCP submit-sprint brief has no max length — GitHub silently truncates beyond 65536 chars
findings.detail: In src/mcp/tools/submit-sprint.ts, the brief field was validated only as z.string().min(1). An MCP client could submit arbitrarily large briefs that GitHub silently truncates.
findings.fix_sketch: Add .max(65000, 'brief must not exceed 65,000 characters (GitHub issue body limit)') to Zod schema. FIXED.

findings.title: statusToEventKind returns string not narrowed union — loses type safety on event kind
findings.detail: In src/agents/verifier/controller.ts, statusToEventKind was typed to return string instead of the narrowed 'verifier.passed' | 'verifier.failed' | 'verifier.timeout' | 'verifier.error' union.
findings.fix_sketch: Narrow return type to the verifier event kind union. FIXED.

findings.title: noopQueue watchForNew stop arrow returns undefined not void — type mismatch
findings.detail: In src/server.ts, noopQueue() implemented watchForNew's stop as () => undefined rather than () => void as the QueueAdapter interface expects.
findings.fix_sketch: Change to stop: (): void => { /* no-op */ } and add explanatory comment. FIXED.

findings.title: Task brief passed as argv to claude subprocess — visible on process list
findings.detail: defaultHaikuCall in auto-router.ts passes the full router prompt (which includes the user-supplied task brief) as a positional CLI argument after --print. On Linux this is visible to all local users via /proc/<pid>/cmdline and ps aux. The inline comment acknowledges this but dismisses it as acceptable; task briefs routinely contain proprietary business context and repo details that should not be world-readable on a shared VPS.
findings.fix_sketch: Pipe the prompt to the child's stdin rather than passing it as an argv token. Use stdio: ['pipe','pipe','pipe'] and child.stdin.write(prompt) to avoid the process-list exposure. The comment claiming stdin was unreliable refers to a race without explicit flush; writing synchronously and then closing stdin resolves it.

findings.title: detectExplicitMode multiline flag matches mode: directive on any body line, not just the header
findings.detail: The regex /^\s*mode\s*:\s*([a-z]+)\s*$/im uses the m (multiline) flag, making ^ and $ match at any line boundary. The intent documented in the JSDoc is to match only a 'Brief body header line', but the regex silently matches 'mode: deslop' embedded anywhere in the task body — including deep in quoted examples or a GitHub issue description. Any user who knows the pattern can override routing by including a bare mode: <value> line anywhere in their issue body.
findings.fix_sketch: Remove the m flag and scan only the first non-empty line: extract firstLine = body.split('\n').find(l => l.trim()), then apply /^\s*mode\s*:\s*([a-z]+)\s*$/i to that line only.

findings.title: buildRetryControlCommand dead export — forceVerifierRetry flag never consumed by control plane
findings.detail: buildRetryControlCommand in retry-orchestrator.ts returns { type: 'sprint_goal', forceVerifierRetry: true, parentTaskId }. A codebase-wide search confirms the function is never called anywhere; the Discord verify_retry button correctly uses { type: 'verify', taskId } instead. The forceVerifierRetry and parentTaskId fields are not handled in parseCommand so if the function were ever called, they would be silently dropped and the result would be a new plain sprint — not a verifier-only retry.
findings.fix_sketch: Remove buildRetryControlCommand entirely — it is dead code that misrepresents how verifier retries work.

findings.title: WorkerRegistry.loadFromDisk zeros worker pool on MaxPlan policy violation with only console.warn
findings.detail: validateMaxPlanConcurrency is called inside the try-catch of loadFromDisk, so when the function throws (e.g. an operator adds a second Max-plan worker to workers.json), the catch block sets this.workers = [] and emits only a console.warn. The daemon continues running with zero workers — no tasks will be dispatched — but the process stays up and appears healthy to PM2. A hot-reload via the FS watcher triggers the same zero-workers outcome silently.
findings.fix_sketch: On a reload (where this.workers already exists), preserve the previous workers value and log the error rather than zeroing. On initial load, throw explicitly for policy violations so the daemon fails fast instead of silently starting with an empty pool.

findings.title: Daemon GitHubQueue constructed with bare unthrottled Octokit, bypassing ThrottledOctokit factory
findings.detail: daemon.ts at line 102 constructs new GitHubQueue(new Octokit({ auth: githubToken }), opts) directly. The factory function createGitHubQueue in src/queue/github.ts wraps Octokit with a throttling+retry plugin (ThrottledOctokit). The direct construction bypasses the plugin: under sustained GitHub Issues polling (the default task source) the daemon's unthrottled client will hit 429s that are not automatically retried, causing pickNext() failures and stalled task ingestion.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace the direct new Octokit(...) + new GitHubQueue(...) with a call to createGitHubQueue(githubToken, opts) or wrap the Octokit instance with the ThrottledOctokit factory before passing it.

findings.title: verify_cancel Discord button kills entire sprint instead of only the verifier step
findings.detail: In interaction-create.ts, the verify_cancel button verb maps to { type: 'cancel', taskId, reason: 'verifier cancelled via discord' } which routes to onCancel and calls orchestrator.cancelSprint(sprintId). This aborts the entire pipeline. An operator clicking the 'Cancel Verify' button after a verifier failure — intending to skip the flaky verification and open the PR anyway — instead cancels the sprint entirely and loses all editor work.
findings.fix_sketch: Map verify_cancel to { type: 'force_pr', taskId } (which already exists as onForcePr) so the operator can skip the verifier and open the PR. Rename the button label to 'Force PR' or add a separate 'Cancel' button alongside so the operator can still fully cancel if desired.

findings.title: extractJsonObject uses lastIndexOf('}') — malformed extraction when reviewer output has trailing braces
findings.detail: extractJsonObject in diff-reviewer.ts finds the first '{' and the LAST '}' to slice the candidate JSON. If the LLM reviewer appends explanatory prose after the JSON object that contains a '}' (e.g. a code snippet or curly-brace commentary), the slice spans from the opening '{' of the JSON through the trailing '}' in the prose, producing an unparseable string. The catch block returns { verdict: 'request_changes', concerns: ['Reviewer JSON malformed...'] }, triggering a spurious fix-review pass on an otherwise-approved diff.
findings.fix_sketch: Use a balanced-brace counter starting from the first '{' to find the matching '}' rather than anchoring to the last '}' in the string. Alternatively, try JSON.parse on progressively narrower end positions until one succeeds.

findings.title: onCancel bare catch swallows all store.updateState errors, not just missing-row misses
findings.detail: In src/orchestrator/handlers/control-plane.ts, the catch block around store.updateState is empty (catch { /* row may not exist yet */ }). This silently absorbs every error including disk full, SQLite corruption, and constraint violations — not just the intended 'row not found' case. When the cancel succeeds in aborting the pipeline but the state transition silently fails, the task remains in_flight in the store and will be recovered as pending on the next daemon restart, potentially re-dispatching a deliberately cancelled task.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace bare catch {} with catch (err) { if (!/no such row|SQLITE_NOTFOUND/i.test(String(err))) console.error('[daemon] updateState failed on cancel:', err); } so unexpected errors are surfaced while the known-safe 'row not found' case is still swallowed.

findings.title: sprint_goal repo field has no length cap in parseCommand unlike all other string fields
findings.detail: In packages/orchestrator-core/src/queue/control-plane.ts, the sprint_goal parse branch applies MAX_ID_FIELD_LEN, MAX_LABEL_LEN, MAX_KEY_LEN, and MAX_GOAL_LEN guards to every string field except repo. An attacker with a valid HMAC secret can supply an arbitrarily long repo string that propagates into store writes, git clone arguments, and RepoResolver allow-list checks — all of which receive the raw unsanitized value.
findings.fix_sketch: Add if (typeof parsed.repo === 'string' && parsed.repo.length > 256) throw new Error('sprint_goal: repo exceeds maximum length') immediately after the repo field is assigned in the sprint_goal parse block.

findings.title: computePressure returns zero pressure for tokensLimit <= 0 API error state
findings.detail: In src/orchestrator/pressure.ts, computePressure returns 0 when headers.tokensLimit <= 0. A pressure of 0 is below PRESSURE_BLOCK_THRESHOLD (0.85), so shouldDispatch() returns true. When the Anthropic API enters a degraded state and reports tokensLimit=0 in rate-limit headers, the daemon treats the worker as fully available and continually dispatches tasks into a failing worker rather than backing off.
findings.fix_sketch: Return 1 (fully pressured / blocked) when tokensLimit <= 0: treat a zero or negative limit as an API error state that should block dispatch until a valid non-zero limit is reported.

findings.title: repoSlugFromUrl extracts only the short repo name, risking collision for repos with identical names
findings.detail: repoSlugFromUrl in verifier/controller.ts takes only the last URL path segment (e.g. 'IFleet' from 'https://github.com/weautomatehq1/IFleet') rather than the full 'owner/name' form. This slug is used to locate invariants directories (.ifleet/invariants/<repoSlug>/). If two repositories managed by the fleet share the same short name (e.g. client-a/api and client-b/api), they would resolve to the same invariants directory, causing cross-contamination of verification rules.
findings.fix_sketch: Capture the last two non-empty path segments: u.pathname.replace(/\.git$/, '').split('/').filter(Boolean).slice(-2).join('-') to get a unique 'owner-name' slug for use in filesystem paths. This is safe for current single-repo usage and correct for multi-repo.

findings.title: buildPrOpener accepts unused _repoRoot parameter that callers pass but is silently discarded
findings.detail: The function signature buildPrOpener(repoId, worktreePath, _repoRoot) includes _repoRoot (prefixed with _ to signal disuse) which is never referenced inside the function body. Callers pass a meaningful value that is silently discarded, creating confusion about whether future path computations should use it.
findings.fix_sketch: Remove the _repoRoot parameter from the signature and update all call sites.

findings.title: ANTHROPIC_VERSION pinned to 2023-06-01 in candidate-gen.ts without a versioning note
findings.detail: The ANTHROPIC_VERSION header is hardcoded to '2023-06-01' in src/agents/proposer/candidate-gen.ts. While Anthropic maintains backward compatibility, the constant has no comment linking to the versioning docs or noting when it was last reviewed. Future maintainers may miss a required update.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a comment: // Anthropic API version — see https://docs.anthropic.com/api/versioning; update when new features are gated behind a newer version.

findings.title: deferringDiscordOut postTaskCreated returns threadId as empty string — falsy sentinel
findings.detail: In src/server.ts, deferringDiscordOut().postTaskCreated returns { threadId: '' }. An empty string is falsy in JavaScript, so callers checking if (result.threadId) treat the deferred case the same as a genuine 'no thread assigned', which could suppress follow-up Discord linking logic silently.
findings.fix_sketch: Return { threadId: undefined } so the deferred case is unambiguously 'not yet assigned'. Alternatively use a sentinel string 'DEFERRED' and document its meaning.

findings.title: resolveTaskIdFromMessage hardcoded to return null with no explanation
findings.detail: In src/orchestrator/daemon.ts, createDiscordClient receives resolveTaskIdFromMessage: async () => null. There is no comment explaining whether this is intentionally unimplemented, permanently unsupported, or a placeholder. Discord message-threading features (replying to a status update to approve/cancel) silently fail to resolve a task ID.
findings.fix_sketch: Add an inline comment: // message-to-task lookup not yet implemented — tasks are found via button customId or slash command taskId option.

findings.title: discardRawLog leaks parent mkdtemp directory on every verifier run
findings.detail: uploadLog creates a temp directory with mkdtempSync and writes verifier.log inside it. discardRawLog only removed the log file, not the parent directory. Under a continuous fleet this is a slow disk-space denial-of-service.
findings.fix_sketch: Added rmSync(dirname(path), { recursive: true, force: true }) after removing the file.

findings.title: extractJsonObject brace-counter ignores string context, corrupts slice on braces in string values
findings.detail: extractJsonObject counted '{' and '}' without tracking whether the current character was inside a JSON string literal. Any verdict payload whose string values contain '{' or '}' could cause premature slice, JSON.parse failure, and a silent misclassification of a passing review as request_changes.
findings.fix_sketch: Added inString/escaped tracking to skip brace counting while inside a quoted JSON string.

findings.title: deferringDiscordOut returns undefined cast to string for threadId, defeating type safety
findings.detail: deferringDiscordOut() returned { threadId: undefined as unknown as string }, a compile-time type lie. The DiscordOut interface required threadId: string, but callers already guarded with if (!result.threadId). The double cast prevented TypeScript from catching unsafe callsites.
findings.fix_sketch: Changed DiscordOut.postTaskCreated return type to Promise<{ threadId: string | undefined }> and removed the cast in deferringDiscordOut().

findings.title: editor.ts forwards full process.env to git subprocesses, exposing secrets to repo hooks
findings.detail: git add, git diff --cached, and git commit in commitEditorChanges inherited process.env containing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, and DISCORD_TOKEN. A malicious repo hook could exfiltrate these.
findings.fix_sketch: Added minimalGitEnv() to all execFileAsync git calls. Exported minimalGitEnv from orchestrator-core.

findings.title: factory.ts forwards full process.env to git push and gh subprocess, exposing secrets
findings.detail: buildPrOpener's git push and gh pr create inherited process.env. A compromised repo's pre-push hook would receive all daemon secrets. The push runs after attacker-controlled code is written to the worktree.
findings.fix_sketch: Used minimalGitEnv() with GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0 auth for git push; minimalGitEnv() + GITHUB_TOKEN for gh commands. Applied minimalGitEnv() to all worktree management git calls.

findings.title: AllAccountsPausedError can carry nextAvailableMs = Infinity when all accounts are permanently banned
findings.detail: soonestRecoveryMs() returned Infinity when all accounts had been auth-banned. A caller using setTimeout(retry, err.nextAvailableMs) would set a timer that never fires, silently stalling the dispatch loop.
findings.fix_sketch: Capped soonestRecoveryMs at Math.min(soonest, 5 * 60_000) so the maximum wait is 5 minutes.

findings.title: withLock uses prev.then(fn, fn) causing fn to run even after predecessor failure
findings.detail: RepoManager.withLock registered fn as both the resolve AND reject handler. If a preceding git operation (clone, fetch) failed, the next queued operation would still run on a potentially corrupted repo state.
findings.fix_sketch: Changed prev.then(fn, fn) to prev.then(fn) so errors propagate and downstream operations are skipped.

findings.title: onVerify handler is fire-and-forget; verification errors are invisible to the HTTP caller
findings.detail: void verifierController.verifyManual(...).catch(console.warn) returned immediately. Operators had no way to distinguish 'verification started' from 'verification silently failed to start'.
findings.fix_sketch: Added broadcastIFleet call in the catch handler so verification failures are surfaced to Discord.

findings.title: IFLEET_PROPOSALS_APPROVER_IDS unset gives generic 'not authorised' error with no actionable hint
findings.detail: When IFLEET_PROPOSALS_APPROVER_IDS was not set, the user received a generic 'You are not authorised' message with no indication the issue was a missing env var.
findings.fix_sketch: Changed error message to explicitly name the missing env var: 'IFLEET_PROPOSALS_APPROVER_IDS is not configured'.

findings.title: sweepCooldowns has dead label guard — paginate already filters by LABEL_IFLEET_COOLDOWN
findings.detail: The guard if (!labelNames.includes(LABEL_IFLEET_COOLDOWN)) continue was unreachable because the paginate call already filtered by that label at the API level.
findings.fix_sketch: Removed the dead guard.

findings.title: verifyManual uses Math.max(...spread) which risks RangeError on large attempt arrays
findings.detail: Math.max(...prior.map(r => r.attempt)) spreads all elements as arguments. On a pathologically large array (>65k entries from a loop bug), this throws a RangeError and verifyManual surfaces an error to operators.
findings.fix_sketch: Replaced with prior.reduce((max, r) => Math.max(max, r.attempt), 0).

findings.title: WorkerRegistry watches file inode, misses atomic-rename writes on Linux inotify
findings.detail: fs.watch(configPath) tracks the inode. Editors and deployment tools that atomically rename a temp file into place create a new inode; the watcher stays on the old one and never fires, silently freezing hot-reload.
findings.fix_sketch: Changed to watch(dirname(configPath), (_event, filename) => { if (filename !== basename(configPath)) return; ... }) so rename events trigger correctly.

findings.title: modes.ts import uses .ts extension, inconsistent with project ESM convention
findings.detail: import type { SprintMode } from '../orchestrator/types.ts' used a .ts extension. The rest of the codebase uses .js extensions for ESM imports.
findings.fix_sketch: Changed to '../orchestrator/types.js'.

findings.title: legacyQueueShim lacks TODO comment explaining when it can be removed
findings.detail: _legacy parameter is intentionally unused but without a comment future readers cannot tell whether the shim is temporary (migration in progress) or permanent.
findings.fix_sketch: Added TODO comment explaining the shim is temporary during GitHubQueue retirement.

findings.title: Empty-string cast '' as SprintId silently misidentifies tasks lacking a sprintId
findings.detail: Using '' as SprintId causes downstream lookups to silently fail on unmatched sprint IDs. Proper fix requires changing SprintId usage to string | undefined in OrchestratorEvent.
findings.fix_sketch: Requires type change to SprintId | undefined in OrchestratorEvent — skipped due to broad impact; filed for follow-up.

findings.title: legacyToUnified seeds ULID with issue creation timestamp, potentially mis-ordering unified store insertions
findings.detail: ulid(legacy.createdAt) encodes GitHub issue creation time in the ULID prefix. During backfill, issues processed in bulk get ULIDs sorted by GitHub creation time rather than insertion order, which can confuse FIFO semantics.
findings.fix_sketch: Change to ulid() (current time) and store createdAt separately — skipped to preserve existing idempotency semantics; filed for follow-up.

findings.title: markFindingsClosed writes index.json outside withClosedJsonLock — crash window leaves index/closed.json inconsistent
findings.detail: markFindingsClosed (batch) calls writeAuditIndex before acquiring withClosedJsonLock, creating a crash window between the two writes. If the process dies after writeAuditIndex but before the withClosedJsonLock block, index.json shows findings as closed/fixed while closed.json has no corresponding records. The singular markFindingClosed correctly holds the lock across both writes (AUDIT-IFleet-d651330f). Batch PR reconciliation during audit-ritual can corrupt the audit trail: findings appear closed in the index but regression detection based on closed.json will not find them.
findings.fix_sketch: Move writeAuditIndex(indexPath, index) inside the withClosedJsonLock callback to be the first statement, eliminating the crash window between the two writes.

findings.title: Empty fingerprint acts as dedup key in appendToClosedJson, silently dropping multiple zero-fingerprint closures
findings.detail: appendToClosedJson and appendClosedRecordUnlocked deduplicate closed.json entries by fingerprint equality. When multiple findings have fingerprint='' (the default when no fingerprint is computed), only the first one is appended — all subsequent ones are silently dropped. Same issue in markFindingsClosed's in-memory alreadyQueued check and existingFingerprints Set.
findings.fix_sketch: Guard fingerprint dedup with a non-empty fingerprint check: only deduplicate when record.fingerprint !== ''. Apply to all three call sites in audit-runner.ts.

findings.title: listActiveSprints in dashboard/server.ts fetches all sprint rows without a LIMIT
findings.detail: The SQL query in listActiveSprints uses ORDER BY updated_at DESC with no LIMIT clause, loading every sprint row from the state DB into memory at once. On a long-running deployment with thousands of completed sprints this could load megabytes of data per dashboard poll cycle.
findings.fix_sketch: Add LIMIT 500 to the SQL query and thread it as a parameter.
